title: Payload adapter and contract negotiator for multi-version usage events
creator: Marco Ruiz
description:
Background:
Redwood's Console backend currently rejects or silently drops some usage events produced by older SDK versions and partner integrations with slight schema drift (field renames, nullable->required flips, and nested array vs object shapes). This ticket implements a lightweight runtime layer — the Payload Adapter and Contract Negotiator — that performs safe transformations and negotiates acceptable event contracts upstream so downstream analytics jobs and SLOs remain stable.

Work done so far:
- Prototype service (payload-adapter-v1) implemented as a sidecar in staging that rewrites three common drift patterns: timestamp string->ISO coercion, legacy "userId"->"actor.id" remapping, and flattening of single-element arrays. Prototype validated against ~12k historical events from staging ingestion.
- Added unit tests for coercion rules and an integration test that runs adapter+validator+consumer pipeline using local stack.
- Observability hooks added: per-rule counters, sample payload sink (rotating), and a metric exposing percentage of adapted events per model and route (metric: ingest.adapt.rate).
- Created design doc: https://confluence.redwood/console/payload-adapter-design (link internal).

Decisions and trade-offs:
- We chose a "weak-typing" default: prefer safe coercions and enrichments over hard rejections to avoid customer-facing errors. Hard rejections only happen for malformed top-level envelopes (missing event_id or timestamp after adaptation).
- Transformation rules are implemented declaratively (YAML rulesets) to allow non-engineering owners to author fixes for minor SDK drift. This trades some performance for maintainability; we mitigate via fast-path bypass if the incoming schema matches the current contract fingerprint.
- We rejected a full schema-evolution engine for now (too heavy) in favor of a staged approach: adapter -> schema-negotiator -> validator, so future iterations can introduce stricter enforcement per-customer or per-route.

Open issues / blockers:
- Need formal approval from Data Security for the sample payload sink behavior (leak risk). Raised to security: ticket SEC-1124.
- Performance fuzz: adapter adds ~4-6ms p95 on staging at current QPS; confirm for 99th at production scale. Load test scheduled 2026-03-15.
- Compatibility mapping for partner X requires legal review for PII field retention.

Next steps (short-term):
- Complete PR and merge payload-adapter service into main branch, PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1427 (in review).
- Add E2E smoke in CI: ingest example event from legacy-sdk with adapter engaged and assert consumer counts.
- Add feature flag gating and per-customer opt-in/opt-out control in the Console config UI (PM scope).
- Run production canary on 10% of routes for 48h with adaptive metrics alerts in case adapt.rate > 8% or error_rate increases.

Acceptance criteria:
- Adapter is deployable as a k8s sidecar or standalone pod and can be toggled via feature flag per-namespace.
- Adapter provides transformation audit logs for every adapted event (sampled) and a metric exposing adapt rate by route and model.
- No increase in consumer schema validation failures after canary; adapt_rate metrics and trace links available in Console.
- Design doc updated with lessons and an API for adding new rulesets.

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood/console/payload-adapter-design
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1427
- Load test plan: https://docs.redwood/ingest/load-tests/payload-adapter
- Related linear tickets: ENG-30218 (incremental-schema-validator), ENG-23601 (schema-compliance-enforcer)

Notes for reviewers:
- Focus on the declarative rules API and the fast-path gating logic. We need a review from runtime for kernel-hot paths and from infra for sidecar resource limits.
- Suggest adding a small quota for sampled payload sinks to avoid S3 billing surprises.

Status update (2026-03-10):
- PR in review, infra approval requested, load test scheduled. Planning canary deployment for 2026-03-20 pending security sign-off.
